title: Plural 1: From One to Many
description: Form the regular nominative plural: hard stems take -ы, soft stems take -и, neuter swaps -о to -а and -е to -я, and after к, г, х, ж, ш, ч, щ the ending is always -и.
descriptionRussian: Именительный падеж множественного числа: твёрдые основы получают -ы, мягкие — -и; средний род меняет -о на -а и -е на -я; после к, г, х, ж, ш, ч, щ всегда пишется -и.
intro: You built these forms back in the A1 noun book. This one takes the plural through all six cases, and the news is better than you would expect: in the plural, gender stops mattering almost immediately. Three of the six cases use a single ending for masculine, feminine and neuter alike. The genitive is the one that fights back, and it gets two lessons.
rules: The plural nominative (множественное число, именительный падеж) answers Кто? (Who?) and Что? (What?) when the noun refers to more than one.
Hard masculine consonants and hard feminine -а stems take -ы: журнал → журналы, мама → мамы, машина → машины.
Soft stems take -и: soft masc -й (трамвай → трамваи), soft masc -ь (словарь → словари), soft fem -я (песня → песни), soft fem -ь (тетрадь → тетради).
The consonants ж, ш, ч, щ and the velars к, г, х never take -ы. They take -и instead. This is the 7-letter spelling rule: карандаш → карандаши, нож → ножи, книга → книги, девочка → девочки.
Neuter -о switches to -а: окно → окна, письмо → письма. Neuter -е switches to -я: море → моря, здание → здания.
Common irregulars to memorise as fixed pairs: дом → дома (stress-shifted -а), брат → братья (the family -ья plural), ребёнок → дети and человек → люди (a completely different word).
examples: В офисе журналы. (There are magazines in the office.) журнал → журналы, hard cons + -ы.
На столе карандаши. (There are pencils on the table.) карандаш → карандаши, ш + -и.
В библиотеке новые словари. (There are new dictionaries in the library.) словарь → словари, soft -ь + -и.
У Ольги красивые машины. (Olga has beautiful cars.) машина → машины, fem hard -а + -ы.
Здесь интересные книги. (Here are interesting books.) книга → книги, velar к + -и (spelling rule).
В комнате большие окна. (There are large windows in the room.) окно → окна, neuter -о → -а.

items.promptEnglish: There are magazines on the table.
items.hint: Singular or plural? Read the English clue.
items.explanation: На столе журнал would mean 'a magazine on the table' (singular). The English plural 'magazines' signals множественное число. Hard masculine consonants take -ы: журнал → журналы.

items.hint: Карандаш ends in ш. Does ш take -ы or -и?
items.explanation: The consonants ж, ш, ч, щ and the velars к, г, х never take -ы. They take -и by the 7-letter spelling rule. Карандаш → карандаши.

items.promptEnglish: There are new dictionaries in the library.
items.hint: Словарь ends in soft -ь. What plural ending does soft take?
items.explanation: Soft stems (-й, -ь, -я) all take -и in the plural. Словарь → словари. Compare with hard masculines like журнал → журналы, where the hard consonant picks the hard vowel -ы.

items.promptEnglish: There are beautiful cars on the street.
items.hint: Машина is feminine in -а. What plural ending follows the hard н before the -а?
items.explanation: Feminine -а stems with a hard consonant before the -а take -ы in the plural: машина → машины, мама → мамы, школа → школы. The hard consonant keeps the noun on the hard track.

items.hint: Compare with машина → машины. Why might книга take a different vowel?
items.explanation: Книга ends in -а, but the consonant before -а is the velar к. After к, г, х you can never write -ы, so the ending switches to -и: книга → книги. Same logic as the carandash question with ш.

items.promptEnglish: There are large windows in the room.
items.hint: Окно is neuter -о. Neuter doesn't take -ы. What does it take?
items.explanation: Neuter -о swaps to -а in the plural: окно → окна, письмо → письма. Neuter -е swaps to -я: море → моря. Watch the stress: окно is end-stressed, but окна shifts the stress to the first syllable.

blanks: В классе новые _____. (There are new desks in the classroom.)
fillInBlank.grammarFocus: Hard masculine consonant + -ы: стол → столы. The English 'desks' signals plural; the hard consonant signals the -ы vowel.

errorCorrection.translationEnglish: There are new pens on the table.
errorCorrection.explanation: A hard feminine -а stem would take -ы in the plural (машина becomes машины), but you can never write -ы after к, г, х and ж, ш, ч, щ. So ручка becomes ручки, not ручкы. Ручкы is not a real Russian form.

errorCorrection.translationEnglish: There are old rubles in the wallet.
errorCorrection.explanation: Рубль is a soft masculine noun ending in -ь, and soft stems take -и in the nominative plural: рубли. The soft sign disappears before the vowel ending, so рубльи with the -ь kept is wrong; рублы applies the hard ending to a soft stem.

errorCorrection.translationEnglish: There are long letters on the table.
errorCorrection.explanation: Neuter nouns do not take -ы or -и in the plural: neuter -о switches to -а. So письмо becomes письма, not письмы. Письмы applies the hard masculine and feminine ending -ы to a neuter noun, which never happens.

minimalPairs.contextEnglish: On the table is/are ___ (one or many?).
minimalPairs.explanation: The English clue 'are' (plus the absence of 'a' / 'one') signals plural. Журналы is the plural nominative of журнал. The singular form журнал would be 'On the table is a magazine.'

Море is neuter -е; in the plural it shifts to моря. The English 'seas' signals plural. Watch the stress shift: singular мо́ре, plural моря́ (the stress moves to the final syllable in many short neuters).

reviewVocab.definition: plural number; the form of a noun, adjective, or verb that refers to more than one
reviewVocab.example: В предложении 'На столе журналы' слово 'журналы' стоит во множественном числе.

reviewVocab.definition: nominative case; the dictionary form of a noun, used for the subject of a sentence
reviewVocab.example: Журналы лежат на столе. (Журналы, the subject, is in the именительный падеж.)

reviewVocab.definition: 7-letter spelling rule: after к, г, х, ж, ш, ч, щ, write -и (not -ы) and -а (not -я). It applies in noun endings, adjective endings, and verb endings.
reviewVocab.example: Книга → книги (not книгы), карандаш → карандаши (not карандашы), девочка → девочки (not девочкы).
